chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: SAQ 1 — Secondary Source (3 points) — Set 2: tea production
chunks.content: AP World History SAQ 1 (Secondary Source), 3 points, one per part. Set 2 prompts: A [1] identify one argument the author makes regarding tea production in the late nineteenth century; B [1] describe one likely reason for the change in tea imports to Britain, as outlined by the author; C [1] explain how one additional piece of evidence NOT in the passage would support/modify the argument. 'Identify' = correct answer; 'Describe' = relevant characteristics; 'Explain' = how/why. Common failure: C naming a piece of evidence without explaining how it bears on the argument.

chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: SAQ 1 Set 2 exemplar — Sample 1A, 3/3
chunks.content: SAQ 1 (Set 2) scored 3/3 (A 1, B 1, C 1). Identified the author's argument, described a reason for the change in tea imports, and explained how an additional piece of evidence would support/modify the argument. Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: SAQ 1 Set 2 exemplar — Sample 1B, 2/3
chunks.content: SAQ 1 (Set 2) scored 2/3 (A 1, B 1, C 0). Identified the argument (A) and described a reason (B) but did not explain how additional evidence would bear on the argument (C). Illustrates losing the Explain part.

chunks.subject: AP World History
chunks.title: SAQ 1 Set 2 exemplar — Sample 1C, 1/3
chunks.content: SAQ 1 (Set 2) scored 1/3 (A 1, B 0, C 0). Identified the argument only. Lost B (no valid reason for the change) and C (no explanation of additional evidence). Illustrates a response confined to reading the source's argument.
